note: Unselected episodic and chronic migraine: fremanezumab, galcanezumab and eptinezumab went to patients on rat/monkey evoked-vasodilation pharmacodynamics and the human CGRP hypothesis, not on a disease model; all three met their Phase 2 and 3 primary endpoints (2014-2020) and all three labels gained a postmarketing hypertension warning in 2025.
label: Migraine (anti-CGRP mAbs)

engagement.model: Rat and cynomolgus evoked neurogenic vasodilation (electrical skin flare, dural artery, capsaicin-induced dermal blood flow), PK/PD-translated to humans
engagement.note: Murine anti-CGRP antibodies (fremanezumab lineage) blocked electrically evoked skin and dural vasodilation in rats for a week; no human readout yet.
engagement.short: Rat flare and dural dilation blocked
engagement.quote: We showed for the first time that anti-CGRP antibodies exert a long lasting inhibition of neurogenic vasodilatation in two different rat models of arterial blood flow.
engagement.judgement: Model opens the track at first use (2008); Zeller's 4901/7E9 are Rinat murine antibodies, the lineage fremanezumab (RN307/LBR-101) came from, so product_in_model is false. The same rat saphenous-flare and dural-window models are in the fremanezumab FDA pharmacology review.

engagement.magnitude_basis: PK/PD-predicted vs observed inhibition of capsaicin-induced dermal blood flow against plasma concentration
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the paper itself states the monkey-to-human comparison. Human CIDBF arm is the Phase 1 study NCT01337596 (Monteith 2017 reports the same readout).
engagement.model: Rat and cynomolgus evoked neurogenic vasodilation (electrical skin flare, dural artery, capsaicin-induced dermal blood flow), PK/PD-translated to humans
engagement.note: Monkey CIDBF PK/PD model correctly predicted inhibition of capsaicin dermal blood flow in healthy volunteers from a single 5 mg SC galcanezumab dose.
engagement.short: Monkey CIDBF PK/PD predicted human CIDBF
engagement.quote: This information was used to generate a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model, which correctly predicted inhibition of capsaicin-induced DBF in humans starting at a single subcutaneous 5-mg dose.
engagement.judgement: readout_tier set to direct: CIDBF is in-vivo blockade of a CGRP-releasing stimulus and the source calls it a target-engagement biomarker; a stricter reader could call blood flow downstream physiology. Healthy volunteers count under the v3 engagement rule.

engagement.confidence_note: Full text read via Europe PMC (PMC6091427). Not in the 2018 fremanezumab PharmR (761089), which predates the paper; no study dosing a member drug and then reading CGRP-evoked cerebral or meningeal arterial relaxation in humans was found, and the galcanezumab capsaicin dermal blood flow readout is a different bed and stimulus, so it is not paired here.
engagement.model: Human ex-vivo cerebral, middle meningeal and abdominal artery rings (wire myograph, CGRP-induced relaxation)
engagement.note: Fremanezumab blocked CGRP-evoked relaxation of human cerebral, meningeal and abdominal artery rings; no member-drug readout of this in dosed humans exists.
engagement.short: Human artery rings, no dosed-human readout
engagement.quote: The aim of the study was to evaluate the in vitro antagonistic effects of fremanezumab on human arteries.
engagement.reason: Readout never measured in dosed humans
engagement.judgement: Ex-vivo blockade of a CGRP stimulus is a direct readout under the engagement rule, but it has never been compared with the same readout in dosed humans, so the cell opens and stays untested rather than being paired with the capsaicin dermal-blood-flow data already on the evoked-vasodilation track.

dose.model: Rat and cynomolgus evoked neurogenic vasodilation (electrical skin flare, dural artery, capsaicin-induced dermal blood flow), PK/PD-translated to humans
dose.note: Rat models gave duration of blockade (a week after one dose) but no human exposure target yet.
dose.short: Rat gives duration, no exposure target
dose.quote: Although CGRP antibody treatment had a slower onset of action than the CGRP receptor antagonists, the inhibition was still evident 1 week after dosing.
dose.judgement: Opens the dose track at model first use; proxy entry on the same system.

dose.magnitude_basis: Model-selected Phase 2 regimen (150 mg q2w, 300 mg/month) vs approved 120 mg/month, 2.5x lower; FDA clinical pharmacology review found no exposure-response between 120 and 240 mg
dose.confidence_note: Paired by me: Vermeersch 2015 states the model set the Phase 2 dose; the patient side is Dodick 2014 (doi 10.1016/S1474-4422(14)70128-0, NCT01625988, 150 mg q2w met the primary endpoint). Abstract-level reading of both.
dose.model: Rat and cynomolgus evoked neurogenic vasodilation (electrical skin flare, dural artery, capsaicin-induced dermal blood flow), PK/PD-translated to humans
dose.note: Retrodiction: the CIDBF PK/PD dose model was first public in 2015, after galcanezumab's own Phase 2 at the model-chosen 150 mg q2w had reported (2014); it reproduces that the regimen was reached and worked.
dose.quote: Utilization of this pharmacodynamic biomarker with pharmacokinetic data collected in phase I studies provided the dose-response relationship that assisted in dose selection for the phase II clinical development of LY2951742.
dose.reason: Model public after drug's own Phase 2
dose.judgement: Scored same under the 'reached, drug worked' row. magnitude records that the model-selected monthly exposure overshot what the clinic needed by about 2.5x (conservative, not wrong). margin_stated true: the FDA pharmacology review (IND 111295 summary) reports monkey 6-month toxicity at 100 mg/kg with no CV, respiratory or CNS findings, far above the 5 mg/kg PD dose, and patients were dosed to target without that toxicity. 2026-11-09 ruling: a dose model first public after the same drug's own patient result is a retrodiction, so same became retro (Vermeersch epub 2015-06-26 vs Dodick 2014 epub 2014-08-10).

efficacy.model: Rat and cynomolgus evoked neurogenic vasodilation (electrical skin flare, dural artery, capsaicin-induced dermal blood flow), PK/PD-translated to humans
efficacy.note: Evoked-vasodilation models read CGRP release, not migraine; Zeller still used them to call the antibody a migraine-prevention candidate.
efficacy.short: Rat dural dilation, no disease model
efficacy.quote: We have provided strong preclinical evidence that anti-CGRP antibody may be a suitable drug candidate for the preventive treatment of migraine.
efficacy.judgement: No disease model existed for the class; the pharmacology package in both 2018 FDA reviews is evoked vasodilation only (CIDBF rat/monkey for galcanezumab; CIDBF monkey, saphenous flare and dural window for fremanezumab).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: Model gives % inhibition of evoked vasodilation, trial gives migraine-day reduction; only direction is comparable
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired by me (Zeller 2008 model, Bigal 2015 HFEM Phase 2b, NCT02025556, epub 2015-09-30); abstract read in full. Earliest public fremanezumab efficacy result is the Teva CM Phase 2b press release of 2015-02-24, same year. The FDA fremanezumab pharmacology review says the relevance of the sponsor's rat models for predicting efficacy is not known.
efficacy.model: Rat and cynomolgus evoked neurogenic vasodilation (electrical skin flare, dural artery, capsaicin-induced dermal blood flow), PK/PD-translated to humans
efficacy.note: Fremanezumab (TEV-48125) 225 and 675 mg monthly cut migraine days vs placebo in the HFEM Phase 2b, the direction the rat model called; Teva's CM Phase 2b release (2015-02-24) was also positive.
efficacy.quote: The LSM difference in the reduction of migraine-days between the placebo and 225 mg dose groups was -2.81 days (95% CI -4.07 to -1.55; p<0.0001)

patient_trials.quote: The least-squares mean (±SE) reduction in the average number of headache days per month was 4.3±0.3 with fremanezumab quarterly, 4.6±0.3 with fremanezumab monthly, and 2.5±0.3 with placebo (P<0.001 for both comparisons with placebo).

efficacy.reason: Direction matched; model reads CGRP, not migraine
efficacy.judgement: Track split per drug: this entry is now the fremanezumab sc track (Zeller's antibodies are fremanezumab's lineage); galcanezumab's Dodick 2014 comparison and eptinezumab's ALD403 Phase 2 were moved to their own appended entries. Scored same: Zeller 2008 made an explicit prospective efficacy prediction and the primary endpoint responded; direction_only because the model has no migraine endpoint.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: Allodynia blocked in rat vs migraine-day reduction in patients
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Epub 2016-05-19, eight months after the TEV-48125 Phase 2b papers (2015-09-30), so a retrodiction. Bree 2018 (epub 2016-12-07, mouse anti-CGRP mAb, post-concussion rat) is the same track and not entered separately.
efficacy.note: Fremanezumab (TEV-48125) blocked trigger-evoked allodynia in rats after Phase 2 had shown efficacy; FDA later filed the model as 'relevance unknown'.
efficacy.short: Rat MOH model reproduces benefit, post hoc
efficacy.quote: These data suggest that acute migraine medications may promote MOH in susceptible individuals through CGRP-dependent mechanisms and that anti-CGRP antibodies may be a useful clinical strategy for the treatment of MOH.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the model was run with the product after the clinic knew the answer and reproduced it, so retro, never same. Registry date is the TEV-48125 HFEM Phase 2b (NCT02025556) it post-dates. The FDA fremanezumab review's 'How relevant these models are for predicting efficacy in human migraine is not known' refers to this model family.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: Neuronal inhibition in rat vs migraine-day reduction in patients
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Mechanism study published 2017-06-22, after Phase 2 (2015) and during Phase 3; its comparison with clinical benefit is stated by the authors. Not found in the FDA review (model_filed null).
efficacy.model: Rat trigeminovascular neuron electrophysiology (dural stimulation, cortical spreading depression)
efficacy.note: Fremanezumab inhibited high-threshold trigeminovascular neurons activated from the dura or by CSD, framed by the authors as explaining the already-known clinical benefit.
efficacy.quote: Clinically, the findings may help to explain the therapeutic benefit of CGRP-mAb in reducing headaches of intracranial origin such as migraine with aura and why this therapeutic approach may not be effective for every migraine patient.
efficacy.judgement: A second retrodiction track: the authors explicitly put the rat result beside the clinical benefit and the non-responder fraction, so comparison_stated true and source_calls_it partial. Scored retro, never same (decision 10).

efficacy.confidence_note: Opener at first use; the same paper supplies the retrodiction entry below.
efficacy.model: Human ex-vivo cerebral, middle meningeal and abdominal artery rings (wire myograph, CGRP-induced relaxation)
efficacy.note: Ex-vivo human artery model first run in 2018, after Phase 3; it reads CGRP vasodilation, not migraine.
efficacy.short: Human artery model opens post hoc
efficacy.quote: The aim of the study was to evaluate the in vitro antagonistic effects of fremanezumab on human arteries.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the efficacy track at model first use (2018), as the brief asks; the model has no migraine endpoint of its own.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: Blockade of CGRP-evoked relaxation in human artery rings vs migraine-day reduction in patients; only direction is comparable
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. Published 2018-08-14, after HALO CM (Silberstein 2017 NEJM, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa1709038, NCT02621931 first posted 2015-12-04) and HALO EM; the paper states the Phase 2 and 3 efficacy as its premise (citing Bigal 2015 and Dodick 2014) but measures no patient outcome itself, so paired by me with model_src the same paper. Registry date is the HALO CM trial it post-dates.
efficacy.model: Human ex-vivo cerebral, middle meningeal and abdominal artery rings (wire myograph, CGRP-induced relaxation)
efficacy.note: Fremanezumab blocked CGRP-induced relaxation in human cerebral, middle meningeal and abdominal arteries, run after HALO had shown efficacy; authors frame it as mechanism.
efficacy.short: Human vessels reproduce benefit, post hoc
efficacy.quote: The antagonistic effect and potency of fremanezumab was similar, suggesting that there are vasodilatory CGRP receptors present in all studied arteries and that the antibody may have effect in all studied vessels.

patient_trials.quote: The least-squares mean (±SE) reduction in the average number of headache days per month was 4.3±0.3 with fremanezumab quarterly, 4.6±0.3 with fremanezumab monthly, and 2.5±0.3 with placebo (P<0.001 for both comparisons with placebo).

efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the product was run in human tissue after the clinic knew the answer and the result was consistent with it, so retro, never same. comparison_stated false because the authors cite the trials as premise rather than placing the two results side by side; source_calls_it null for the same reason. Kept at direction_only: an ex-vivo relaxation shift cannot be set against migraine days.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Europe PMC full text returned HTTP 500). model_filed null: the eptinezumab PharmR (761119) is not in the bundle and the FDA download was blocked; the 761119 SumR nonclinical section lists only toxicology studies, and the 761063 and 761089 PharmRs have no mouse photophobia model.
efficacy.model: Mouse CGRP-injection-evoked light aversion and spontaneous pain (grimace/squint)
efficacy.note: CGRP-injected mice show light aversion; the model was first run with an Alder anti-CGRP antibody after the ALD403 Phase 2 had read out.
efficacy.short: Mouse photophobia model opens post hoc
efficacy.quote: To address the role of CGRP both within and outside the CNS, we used CGRP-induced light-aversive behavior in mice as a measure of migraine-associated photophobia.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the track at first use with an anti-CGRP antibody (2017); CGRP-evoked light aversion in mice existed earlier (Recober 2009, central CGRP in nestin/hRAMP1 mice) but had not been run with an antibody of this class.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: Attenuation of CGRP-evoked light aversion in mice vs migraine-day reduction in patients; only direction is comparable
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the abstract names only 'a CGRP-blocking monoclonal antibody', its identity as ALD405 (Alder, eptinezumab's murine sibling) comes from the checker's reading of the full text. Published 2017-01-04, after the ALD403 Phase 2 (Dodick 2014 Lancet Neurol, doi 10.1016/S1474-4422(14)70209-1, NCT01772524 first posted 2013-01-21), whose registry date is used. Rea 2018 Pain (doi 10.1097/j.pain.0000000000001337, PMID 29994995) ran the same antibody in the CGRP-evoked squint/grimace arm of this system with the same result and is not entered separately.
efficacy.model: Mouse CGRP-injection-evoked light aversion and spontaneous pain (grimace/squint)
efficacy.note: A CGRP-blocking antibody (ALD405, eptinezumab's murine sibling) blocked CGRP-evoked light aversion in mice, three years after ALD403 Phase 2 had shown benefit.
efficacy.quote: Importantly, two clinically effective migraine drugs, the 5-HT1B/D agonist sumatriptan and a CGRP-blocking monoclonal antibody, attenuated the peripheral CGRP-induced light aversion and motility behaviors.

patient_trials.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was the change from baseline to weeks 5-8 in the frequency of migraine days, as recorded in patient electronic diaries.

efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the authors call the antibody a 'clinically effective migraine drug' and use the model to test where CGRP acts, so the model reproduced a result already known from patients; retro, never same. product_in_model false because ALD405 is a sibling of eptinezumab, not the product. comparison_stated false: the trials are cited as premise, not set against the model data.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (no PMC record). model_filed null: the eptinezumab PharmR (761119) is not in the bundle and the FDA download was blocked; GTN appears in the 761089 PharmR only as the trigger in the post-concussion model, not as a model of its own.
efficacy.model: Mouse glyceryl-trinitrate-provoked and rat spontaneous-trigeminal-allodynia migraine-like pain (cutaneous mechanical hypersensitivity)
efficacy.note: Mouse GTN-provoked and rat spontaneous trigeminal-allodynia models first run with an anti-CGRP antibody in 2019, after eptinezumab's Phase 3s had reported.
efficacy.short: GTN and STA models open post hoc
efficacy.quote: Cutaneous sensitivity to hind paw, and periorbital mechanical stimulation were used as surrogate markers of activation of relevant pain pathways in each respective model.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the track at first use with an antibody of this class (2019). The mouse GTN model and the selectively bred spontaneous-allodynia rat are two paradigms run in one paper with one result, kept as one track to avoid duplicate rows; a later paper separating them would split it.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: Relief of cutaneous mechanical hypersensitivity in rodents vs migraine-day reduction in patients; only direction is comparable
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Published 2019-07-09, after eptinezumab PROMISE-1 (NCT02559895 first posted 2015-09-25; Ashina 2020 Cephalalgia doi 10.1177/0333102420905132) and PROMISE-2 had reported positive, so a retrodiction; registry date is PROMISE-1. The olcegepant arm is a sibling class (CGRP receptor antagonist) and is not scored. Paired by me with model_src the same paper.
efficacy.model: Mouse glyceryl-trinitrate-provoked and rat spontaneous-trigeminal-allodynia migraine-like pain (cutaneous mechanical hypersensitivity)
efficacy.note: ALD405 (eptinezumab's sibling) relieved mechanical hypersensitivity in GTN-provoked mice and spontaneous-allodynia rats, run after PROMISE-1 and PROMISE-2 had read out positive.
efficacy.short: Rodent pain models reproduce known benefit
efficacy.quote: Olcegepant and ALD405 significantly alleviated cutaneous mechanical hypersensitivity in both models compared with corresponding control treatments (saline and IgG control antibody respectively).

patient_trials.quote: Eptinezumab 100 mg and 300 mg met the primary endpoint, significantly reducing MMDs across weeks 1-12 compared with placebo (30 mg, -4.0; 100 mg, -3.9, p = 0.0182; 300 mg, -4.3; placebo, -3.2, p = 0.0001).

efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the authors' stated purpose is to validate the models against a class already known to work ('confirming that translationally-relevant disease mechanisms are engaged'), so the models reproduced a known patient result; retro, never same. product_in_model false (ALD405 is eptinezumab's sibling). The abstract's 'potential clinical utility ... in the abortive treatment of migraine' is a forward prediction for an indication no member drug has tested and is not scored.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: Model gives % inhibition of evoked vasodilation, trial gives migraine-day change; the predicted benefit was absent (LS mean difference -0.1 day, 95% CI -1.48 to 1.22)
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired by me (Zeller 2008 model, Teva pediatric CM trial). Results first posted on ClinicalTrials.gov 2025-12-19 (tier 3: LS mean difference -0.1, p=0.8484), which dates the entry; the AAN 2026 abstract (Hershey et al., Neurology supplement) is the src, abstract read in full. Whether a pediatric chronic-migraine miss scores against an adult-derived Unselected track is checker rule question 1; the companion pediatric EM trial NCT04458857 met its primary.
efficacy.model: Rat and cynomolgus evoked neurogenic vasodilation (electrical skin flare, dural artery, capsaicin-induced dermal blood flow), PK/PD-translated to humans
efficacy.note: Fremanezumab missed its primary in children and adolescents with chronic migraine (6-17 y), against the class benefit the rat model called; pediatric EM was positive. Children and adolescents with migraine are patients of the context disease (Unselected).
efficacy.quote: Fremanezumab significantly reduced MMD versus placebo (–2.5 vs –1.4; p=0.0210) in the EM study; no significant difference was observed between treatment groups in the CM study (–3.8 vs –3.7; p=0.8484).

patient_trials.quote: Fremanezumab significantly reduced MMD versus placebo (–2.5 vs –1.4; p=0.0210) in the EM study

efficacy.reason: Member drug missed placebo-controlled primary in pediatric CM
efficacy.judgement: Scored contra because a member drug missed its placebo-controlled primary endpoint in patients of the context disease (Unselected population includes children), and one drug's contra beats the adult same on this track; the positive pediatric EM study is recorded under patient_trials.

efficacy.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: the galcanezumab IND 111295 nonclinical package was reviewed 2011-04-04 (761063 PharmR); the model data were first public in Vermeersch 2015 (abstract read).
efficacy.model: Rat and cynomolgus evoked neurogenic vasodilation (electrical skin flare, dural artery, capsaicin-induced dermal blood flow), PK/PD-translated to humans
efficacy.note: Galcanezumab (LY2951742) run in the evoked-vasodilation system before first-in-human; it reads CGRP activity, not migraine.
efficacy.quote: To support the clinical development of LY2951742, capsaicin-induced dermal blood flow (DBF) was used as a target engagement biomarker to assess CGRP activity in nonhuman primates and healthy volunteers.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the galcanezumab track on this system at its first use for that drug (2011 proxy), appended so existing indices stay valid.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: Model gives % inhibition of evoked vasodilation, trial gives migraine-day reduction; only direction is comparable
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired by me (Zeller 2008 model, Dodick 2014 galcanezumab Phase 2, NCT01625988, epub 2014-08-10); abstract-level reading. The FDA fremanezumab pharmacology review (2018) says of the sponsor's rat models 'How relevant these models are for predicting efficacy in human migraine is not known'.
efficacy.model: Rat and cynomolgus evoked neurogenic vasodilation (electrical skin flare, dural artery, capsaicin-induced dermal blood flow), PK/PD-translated to humans
efficacy.note: Galcanezumab 150 mg q2w cut migraine headache days 1.2 days vs placebo in Phase 2, the direction the rat model called; Phase 3s agreed.
efficacy.quote: The mean change from baseline to week 12 in the number of migraine headache days was -4·2 (SD 3·1; 62·5% decrease) in the LY2951742 group compared with -3·0 (SD 3·0; 42·3% decrease) in the placebo group

patient_trials.quote: The mean change from baseline to week 12 in the number of migraine headache days was -4·2 (SD 3·1; 62·5% decrease) in the LY2951742 group compared with -3·0 (SD 3·0; 42·3% decrease) in the placebo group
treatment with galcanezumab significantly reduced monthly migraine headache days (both P < .001) by 4.7 days (120 mg) and 4.6 days (240 mg) compared with placebo (2.8 days).

efficacy.reason: Direction matched; model reads CGRP, not migraine
efficacy.judgement: Split from the former efficacy 2 (now fremanezumab): the galcanezumab sc track on this system. Scored same because Zeller 2008 made an explicit prospective efficacy prediction and the primary endpoint responded; EVOLVE-1 (2018) agreed. direction_only: the model has no migraine endpoint.

efficacy.confidence_note: The eptinezumab FDA summary review lists only toxicology as nonclinical work; the opener sits at the model's class prediction (Zeller 2008), abstract read.
efficacy.model: Rat and cynomolgus evoked neurogenic vasodilation (electrical skin flare, dural artery, capsaicin-induced dermal blood flow), PK/PD-translated to humans
efficacy.note: Rat evoked-vasodilation class prediction (2008) stands for eptinezumab; no ALD403 run in this system was found.
efficacy.quote: We have provided strong preclinical evidence that anti-CGRP antibody may be a suitable drug candidate for the preventive treatment of migraine.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the eptinezumab iv track at the model's first use for the class, since no eptinezumab-specific use was found; appended so existing indices stay valid.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: Model gives % inhibition of evoked vasodilation, trial gives migraine-day reduction; only direction is comparable
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired by me (Zeller 2008 model, Dodick 2014b ALD403 Phase 2, NCT01772524, epub 2014-10-05); abstract read in full. Exploratory proof-of-concept trial whose primary objective was safety; efficacy endpoint tested one-sided.
efficacy.model: Rat and cynomolgus evoked neurogenic vasodilation (electrical skin flare, dural artery, capsaicin-induced dermal blood flow), PK/PD-translated to humans
efficacy.note: A single 1000 mg IV dose of ALD403 (eptinezumab) cut migraine days vs placebo at weeks 5-8 (one-sided p=0.0306), the direction the rat model called; PROMISE-1 (2017) agreed.
efficacy.quote: The mean change in migraine days between baseline and weeks 5-8 was -5·6 (SD 3·0) for the ALD403 group compared with -4·6 (3·6) for the placebo group (difference -1·0, 95% CI -2·0 to 0·1; one-sided p=0·0306).

patient_trials.quote: Eptinezumab 100 mg and 300 mg met the primary endpoint, significantly reducing MMDs across weeks 1-12 compared with placebo (30 mg, -4.0; 100 mg, -3.9, p = 0.0182; 300 mg, -4.3; placebo, -3.2, p = 0.0001).

efficacy.reason: Direction matched; model reads CGRP, not migraine
efficacy.judgement: Split from the former efficacy 2: the eptinezumab iv track. Scored same on the primary efficacy endpoint (one-sided p=0.0306, as pre-specified); direction_only because the model has no migraine endpoint.

safety.model: Rat chronic blood pressure and heart rate under anti-CGRP antibody; monkey safety pharmacology
safety.note: Rats on chronic anti-CGRP antibody showed no change in heart rate or blood pressure: a stated prediction of no cardiovascular harm.
safety.short: Rat predicts no BP or HR change
safety.quote: Chronic treatment with anti-CGRP antibodies had no detectable effects on heart rate or blood pressure.
safety.judgement: The model made an explicit null prediction on blood pressure, which is what the later entries test. FDA monkey 6-week and 6-month safety pharmacology (galcanezumab review) made the same null prediction with the product.

safety.magnitude_basis: Null effect on BP and HR in rats vs no clinically relevant BP, HR or ECG change in dosed humans
safety.confidence_note: Paired by me (Zeller 2008 rat null prediction vs LBR-101 Phase 1 hemodynamics); abstract-level reading. NCT for the LBR-101 Phase 1 studies not found in the abstract, registry_date left null.
safety.model: Rat chronic blood pressure and heart rate under anti-CGRP antibody; monkey safety pharmacology
safety.note: LBR-101 (fremanezumab) up to 2000 mg produced no clinically relevant BP, HR or ECG change over three months in healthy women over 40.
safety.short: No BP, HR or ECG change in humans
safety.quote: Sustained CGRP inhibition was not associated with hemodynamic or ECG changes in a population at an increased age risk for cardiovascular events.
safety.judgement: Healthy volunteers count. product_in_model false because the rat prediction used Zeller's murine precursors, not fremanezumab itself; the FDA-filed monkey safety pharmacology did use the product.

safety.magnitude_basis: Null CV prediction vs CV SAE incidence indistinguishable from placebo
safety.confidence_note: Trials excluded significant cardiovascular disease, so the null is in a low-risk population; FDA explicitly said the healthy-animal data do not address ischaemia.
safety.model: Rat chronic blood pressure and heart rate under anti-CGRP antibody; monkey safety pharmacology
safety.note: Galcanezumab Phase 3 pool: cardiovascular serious adverse events 0.3%, 0% and 0.1% on 240 mg, 120 mg and placebo; no CV postmarketing study required.
safety.short: Patient CV SAEs flat vs placebo
safety.quote: The incidence of cardiovascular serious adverse events was similar in all 3 treatment groups: 0.3%, 0%, and 0.1% for galcanezumab 240 mg, galcanezumab 120 mg, and placebo, respectively.
safety.judgement: First entry of the galcanezumab sc track: the Phase 3 pool matched the models' null cardiovascular prediction (FDA-filed monkey safety pharmacology used the product).

safety.magnitude_basis: Predicted null blood-pressure effect vs new-onset or worsened hypertension in patients
safety.confidence_note: de Vries Lentsch 2022 Neurology (PMID 36195452, epub 2022-10-04), abstract read; Leiden cohort, fremanezumab n=87 beside erenumab (outside the class). Rule 6 earliest date per checker adjudication; the Ajovy label warning (761089s030, 2025-03-21; quote also in s031) confirms.
safety.model: Rat chronic blood pressure and heart rate under anti-CGRP antibody; monkey safety pharmacology
safety.note: Systolic blood pressure rose on fremanezumab in a prospective migraine cohort (2022), and FDA added a hypertension warning to the Ajovy label on 2025-03-21; the rat and monkey models had predicted no BP effect.
safety.quote: For fremanezumab (n = 87), systolic but not diastolic BP was increased compared with T0 at T1 (p = 0.006) and T2 (p = 0.004).
safety.reason: Model said no BP effect; hypertension warning
safety.judgement: Blood pressure is a harm rats and monkeys can show, and the model stated a null, so the contradiction scores contra on this track rather than being set aside; confidence medium because the human signal is postmarketing and confounded. Raynaud's phenomenon and constipation were added at the same time but are not scored: neither species readout was stated for them. Same->contra needs no patient_signal_reversed flag. Year moved 2025 -> 2022 under rule 6 (checker adjudication): the fremanezumab arm of de Vries Lentsch 2022 is the earliest public patient BP rise for this drug.

safety.magnitude_basis: Predicted null blood-pressure effect vs new-onset or worsened hypertension in patients
safety.confidence_note: Safety labeling change dated 2025-03-21 on Drugs@FDA; quote read from the current Emgality label text (openFDA), section 5.3. No earlier galcanezumab patient BP signal found.
safety.model: Rat chronic blood pressure and heart rate under anti-CGRP antibody; monkey safety pharmacology
safety.note: FDA added a hypertension warning to the Emgality label on 2025-03-21 from postmarketing reports; the rat and monkey models had predicted no blood-pressure effect.
safety.quote: Development of hypertension and worsening of pre-existing hypertension have been reported following the use of CGRP antagonists, including EMGALITY, in the postmarketing setting.
safety.reason: Model said no BP effect; hypertension warning
safety.judgement: Split from the former safety 4 (now fremanezumab): blood pressure is a harm rats and monkeys can show and the model stated a null, so the postmarketing warning is contra on this track.

safety.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: the toxicology preceded the ALD403 Phase 2 (NCT01772524 posted 2013-01-21); first public in the 2020 FDA summary review (bundle text read).
safety.model: Rat chronic blood pressure and heart rate under anti-CGRP antibody; monkey safety pharmacology
safety.note: Rat and monkey toxicology with safety pharmacology found no adverse effects of IV eptinezumab: a null cardiovascular prediction.
safety.quote: No adverse effects of IV eptinezumab were observed in either the rat 4-week or monkey 6-month general toxicology studies; the no observed adverse effect levels (NOAELs) were determined to be 100 mg/kg/week and 150 mg/kg every 2 weeks, respectively.
safety.judgement: Opens the eptinezumab iv track at the model's first use for that drug (proxy 2013); appended so existing indices stay valid.

safety.magnitude_basis: Null BP/HR effect in rats vs no vital-sign difference in patients
safety.confidence_note: Paired by me (Zeller 2008 rat null BP prediction, Dodick 2014b NCT01772524); abstract read in full.
safety.model: Rat chronic blood pressure and heart rate under anti-CGRP antibody; monkey safety pharmacology
safety.note: ALD403 (eptinezumab) 1000 mg IV in migraine patients: no vital-sign differences from placebo, as the models' null cardiovascular prediction said.
safety.quote: There were no differences in vital signs or laboratory safety data between the two treatment groups.
safety.judgement: The rat model's stated null cardiovascular effect is a safety prediction; the eptinezumab Phase 2 matched it.

safety.magnitude_basis: Predicted null blood-pressure effect vs new-onset or worsened hypertension in patients
safety.confidence_note: Safety labeling change dated 2025-03-21 on Drugs@FDA; quote read from the current Vyepti label text (openFDA), section 5.3. No earlier eptinezumab patient BP signal found.
safety.model: Rat chronic blood pressure and heart rate under anti-CGRP antibody; monkey safety pharmacology
safety.note: FDA added a hypertension warning to the Vyepti label on 2025-03-21 from postmarketing reports; the rat and monkey models had predicted no blood-pressure effect.
safety.quote: Development of hypertension and worsening of pre-existing hypertension have been reported following the use of CGRP antagonists, including VYEPTI, in the postmarketing setting.
safety.reason: Model said no BP effect; hypertension warning
safety.judgement: Split from the former safety 4 (now fremanezumab): blood pressure is a harm rats and monkeys can show and the model stated a null, so the postmarketing warning is contra on this track.
